title: memory-awareness DB recall has NO cheap-prompt cache: every qualifying prompt (>=15 chars, not slash) pays the full daemon-probe + 2 uv subprocesses, even for back-to-back identical or trivial intents — unlike heartbeat which has a 30s cache guard
observe_how: Submit the same prompt twice; memory-recall.jsonl shows two full-cost fires (no dedupe/TTL). Contrast heartbeat.ts shouldUpdateHeartbeat 30s cache that skips the DB write.
telemetry: memory-recall.jsonl logs one full-cost row per qualifying prompt regardless of repetition; no cache key recorded.

title: Every Postgres-backed UserPromptSubmit hook pays uv-run cold start (~2.2s) PER QUERY: db-utils-pg.runPgQuery and memory-awareness both shell out to `uv run python` rather than holding a connection — the uv interpreter startup, not the SQL, is the dominant cost
observe_how: Time `uv run python -c 'pass'` cold (~2s) vs the actual asyncpg.connect+query (~50-100ms on localhost); the ratio shows ~95% of heartbeat/recall DB latency is interpreter startup.
telemetry: runPgQuery timeout is 3000ms (line 71); the comment 'reduced for faster startup' confirms uv startup is the bottleneck being fought, not query time.

title: sentry-error-context is registered as a SECOND separate UserPromptSubmit block (own process spawn) yet early-exits as a pure no-op unless SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_DSN are set — a guaranteed Node spawn + stdin read with zero effect on this machine
observe_how: Check env: SENTRY_ORG/SENTRY_DSN are unset (not in settings.json env block), so handleUserPrompt is never reached — the hook reads stdin, checks two env vars, prints '{}'. Payoff: removing it drops one process spawn per prompt for no behavior loss.
telemetry: Hook prints '{}' unconditionally when both Sentry env vars are unset; no telemetry but the early-exit branch is deterministic.
